title: Charles I and Nicholas to Sir William Boswell, 2 Nov 1643, TNA SP 84/157 ff. 217, 219

steps.what: Pitt's repository found with the alphabet; TNA references from Discovery; Simpson 1893 re-credentials letter and memorial, CSPD.
Pitt's row against 20,000 random rows over the same periodic structure: z = 9.6, 0 of 20,000 as good.
Free 24-letter row annealed for periods 20-32; over-fits at 106 letters, not decisive.
The four graphic signs are word-signs introduced inline: good, Cousin, Master, us.

Addressee identified as the Duke of Courland's envoy from Simpson's re-credentials letter of the same day; arms shipment matches CSPD.

texts.label: Charles I, Oxford, 2 Nov 1643, TNA SP 84/157 f. 217
texts.summary: Not a letter to Boswell but to the Duke of Courland's envoy at The Hague: Charles I thanks the Duke for his offers, asks for his assistance with arms, muskets, match and powder shipped to Weymouth, Dartmouth, Exeter, Falmouth or another port, and sends the envoy his re-credentials. The transcription is Tomokiyo's provisional one (no images online).

texts.label: Nicholas to Boswell, 2 Nov 1643, TNA SP 84/157 f. 219
texts.summary: Secretary Nicholas tells Boswell to hinder secretly the coming over of [ambassadors?] from the [States?], thought not to affect monarchy, and that the King's two letters are put into Boswell's cipher for him to decipher and interpret for the envoy; 'Monsieur F I R X S S' (probably Firks, the Duke's agent) has not appeared.
